idiom_name: wrapper class over httpx.Client with a per-instance cache
implementation_notes: The delegate is a plain class (or module of functions) that owns one httpx.Client - which pools connections and carries base_url/timeout/header defaults - and exposes domain-shaped methods; response.raise_for_status() plus a mapped exception hierarchy replaces the remote API's exception types, and the lookup cache becomes a per-instance dict (be careful with functools.lru_cache on methods). Generated gRPC stubs are the library alternative when an IDL exists, but they are still wrapped by a hand-written class to keep transport types out of callers. Aggregation and amortized lookups are the reasons to keep the wrapper rather than calling the generated client directly.
pitfalls: httpx.Client is thread-safe but not asyncio-safe; an AsyncClient belongs to one event loop and must be closed with the context manager.
Letting only httpx.TransportError be translated while HTTPStatusError escapes couples callers to the library's exception model.
An unbounded per-instance cache keeps stale invoices and pins memory, and lru_cache applied to an instance method keeps the instance alive forever.
A module-level client created at import time breaks test isolation and can bind a stale event loop.
